title: The TAK Server side
breadcrumb: Wire up Deploy App TAK Servers via a Federation Hub (IaC)

headings.text: Groups are already wired to Keycloak

blocks.html:
Most of this is already done by Deploy App's CoreConfig.tpl. Your IaC adds two small, templated things: the hub's CA (for trust) and, only if the servers initiate the connection, an outgoing federation entry.

What's already in the template

Deploy App's CoreConfig.tpl renders (with env substitution) a federation-ready server:

<federation allowFederatedDelete="false" allowMissionFederation="true"
            allowDataFeedFederation="true"
            enableMissionFederationDisruptionTolerance="true"
            missionFederationDisruptionToleranceRecencySeconds="43200"
            enableFederation="true" ... >
  <federation-server port="9000" coreVersion="2"
                     v1enabled="false" v2port="9001" v2enabled="true"
                     webBaseUrl="https://{{.Env.TAK_SERVER_ADDRESS}}:8443/Marti">
    <tls keystoreFile="certs/files/takserver.jks"
         truststoreFile="certs/files/fed-truststore.jks" .../>   <!-- the fed truststore -->
    <federation-token-authentication enabled="true" tls="true" port="9002"/>
  </federation-server>
  <fileFilter><fileExtension>pref</fileExtension></fileFilter>     <!-- blocks .pref crossing -->
</federation>

So you already have federation enabled, v2 on 9001, token auth on 9002, MFDT on, and a .pref file blocker. Leave all of it in place.

What your IaC injects

  1. Trust the hub. Drop the hub's CA PEM into /ca_public/ (for example fedhub_ca.pem) before first run, so it's imported into fed-truststore.jks (see the trust model). This is the only trust change needed if the hub initiates the connection.

  2. Optional outgoing entry. If you want the server to initiate to the hub instead, template a <federation-outgoing> inside <federation> pointing at the hub's v2 port (9102):

    <federation-outgoing displayName="central-hub" port="9102"
                     address="{{.Env.FEDHUB_ADDRESS}}" protocolVersion="2"
                     reconnectInterval="30" enabled="true"/>

Who initiates

Either side can open the connection; only one should. For IaC across many deployments, let the hub initiate (an Outgoing node in the hub policy connects to each server's 9001). Then each server needs no per-hub config, only the hub CA in its trust store, and the hub is the single place that holds the topology.

Groups are already wired to Keycloak

The template's <auth default="ldap" x509groups="true" x509addAnonymous="false"> means a federate or client cert's CN becomes the username, which is looked up in LDAP for its groups. LDAP is backed by Keycloak/RASENMAEHER, and groups are named tak_<group> (the tak_ prefix is stripped, so TAK sees <group>). That <group> name is what the hub's federation filtering matches, which is the next page.
